profile.summary: ProtCell is a foundation model for single-cell proteomics, where assays such as CITE-seq and CyTOF measure different, limited protein panels. It takes a cell's protein abundance profile over whatever panel was measured and learns cell- and protein-level representations, used for cell annotation, batch integration, imputing unmeasured proteins and choosing compact protein panels.

summary_quotes.text: targeted assays measure limited and non-identical protein panels, fragmenting information across experiments
ProtCell combines protein-identity and continuous-abundance embeddings in a transformer encoder and learns cell- and protein-level representations through masked abundance modeling
It connects fragmented profiles through cell annotation and integration, extends them through protein imputation and inference, and guides the selection of informative protein panels.

sections.title: How it works
sections.body: Each measured protein is represented by a protein-identity embedding from a shared protein codebook plus a continuous embedding of its abundance. A transformer encoder (in the CUDA configuration: 8 layers, model width 256, 8 heads, feed-forward size 2048) is pre-trained by masking abundances (masked ratio 0.15) and reconstructing them with a mean squared error loss; a CLS token feeds the decoder. Inputs are CITE-seq data normalised by CLR or CyTOF data with ARCSIN preprocessing.

quotes.text: using a protein codebook, continuous-abundance embeddings and masked language modeling

sections.title: Versions and reproducibility
sections.body: Release v1.0.0 (published 11 October 2026) holds protcell_pretrained.pt and protcell_pretrained_moore.pt (each 53,226,872 bytes), a sidecar JSON recording that protcell_pretrained.pt comes from large-scale-new-10/model_369999.pt with its SHA-256, a SHA256SUMS file and an example data archive. large-scale-new-10 is also the experiment name in the CUDA configuration. The model was pre-trained on Moore Threads MTT S5000 GPUs; the sources do not explain how the _moore checkpoint differs. A result should name the checkpoint file and its SHA-256.

sections.title: Intended uses
sections.body: Batch integration and clustering, cell type annotation and annotation transfer, reconstruction of masked protein abundances, inference of unmeasured proteins, and protein panel selection; each has a notebook in the repository.

quotes.text: Batch integration, clustering and UMAP visualization.
Inference and analysis of unmeasured proteins.

facts.label: Model type
facts.value: Transformer encoder foundation model for single-cell proteomics.

facts.label: Architecture
facts.value: Transformer encoder with protein-identity and continuous-abundance embeddings; CUDA config: 8 layers, d_model 256, 8 heads, feed-forward 2048, hidden_dim 512, dropout 0.15.

facts.label: Inputs
facts.value: AnnData files with harmonised protein names in var_names, nonnegative abundances, and technology and preprocessing marked as CITE-seq/CLR or CyTOF/ARCSIN; proteins mapped through the provided vocabulary.

quotes.text: Prepare preprocessed AnnData (`.h5ad`) files with harmonized protein names in `adata.var_names`.
The training loader expects nonnegative abundances and treats negative values as invalid.

run_guide.summary: Clone the repository, install the dependencies for a CUDA environment, download the v1.0.0 checkpoint and example data, and open the task notebooks.
prerequisites: Python 3.10 and a CUDA-enabled PyTorch environment (or Moore Threads MUSA).
Disk for the example data archive (966,607,510 bytes).

steps.title: Get the code and install
steps.shell:
git clone https://github.com/hubwenbwen/ProtCell.git
cd ProtCell
git checkout --detach 273d6ca8d4f47c9258fb6db747a0dd8f114a13c7
python -m pip install -r requirements.txt
python -c "import torch; print(torch.cuda.is_available())"
steps.explanation: The README's clone and CUDA install commands; the checkout line is added by Rewire to pin the reviewed commit. The last line should print True.
steps.source_locator: README.md: Environment setup; Pretraining on NVIDIA GPUs

steps.title: Download checkpoint and example data
steps.shell:
# Download protcell_example_data.tar.gz, protcell_pretrained.pt and protcell_pretrained.json from https://github.com/hubwenbwen/ProtCell/releases/tag/v1.0.0 into the repository root
tar -xzf protcell_example_data.tar.gz
mkdir -p checkpoints
mv protcell_pretrained.pt protcell_pretrained.json checkpoints/
steps.explanation: The README says to download the three files from the v1.0.0 release page; the tar and mv lines are the README's.
steps.source_locator: README.md: Data and pretrained model; release v1.0.0

steps.title: Run the notebooks
steps.shell:
python -m ipykernel install --user --name protein_llm --display-name "ProtCell (Python 3.10)"
jupyter lab
steps.explanation: Registers the kernel named in the README and starts Jupyter; open results/Annotation.ipynb or another task notebook.
